data.completion_memo: Implemented cross-project lifecycle rule templates stored in app settings. Added settings-backed RuleTemplate storage with normalization, save/delete helpers, and legacy settings compatibility; added Tauri commands to save a selected project rule as a template, create a normal project-local rule from a selected template, and delete templates without touching project SQLite. Dashboard and app settings payloads now include rule templates. Extended the Rules workspace with template selection, save/create/delete controls, while fixed hook prompts remain separate. Added Rust tests for settings normalization/save/delete and template-to-rule insertion. Verified with cargo check, cargo test, git diff --check, and npm run build outside the sandbox after the known Vite/esbuild spawn EPERM sandbox failure.

lines:
Add reusable rule templates for the Rules workspace.

Requirements:
- Store rule templates in application settings (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Adashi\settings.json`), not in the project SQLite database, so templates are shared across projects.
- A template should capture the editable project rule fields needed to recreate a rule: name, enabled/default enabled state, intend, hook, and prompt. Include stable template ids and timestamps in settings for reliable UI operations.
- Add Tauri/Rust command support to list templates in dashboard/settings payloads, save an existing project rule as a template, create a project-local rule from a template, and delete a template.
- Creating from a template must insert a normal project rule into the active project DB and bump the project revision through the existing rule creation path.
- Saving/deleting templates must update application settings only; do not create project DB tables for templates.
- Extend the Rules UI with simple controls to save the selected rule as a template, create a rule from a selected template, and delete a template. No template editing UI is required.
- Preserve fixed hook prompts as Settings-managed hooks and keep them out of optional rule templates unless a user explicitly creates a normal project rule from a template.
- Verify with focused Rust tests for settings normalization/save/delete/template-to-rule behavior where practical, plus `cargo check` and the frontend build if available.

data.title: Implement cross-project rule templates stored in app settings
